methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort study with small sample (n=44) and no external validation. Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and appropriate patient selection documented. Leave-one-out cross-validation reasonable for sample size, but lacks independent external validation cohort. Multiple statistical tests conducted with Bonferroni correction applied. Authors acknowledge limitations including small sample size, single-center design, and metal artifact uncertainties affecting dose calculations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study addressing clinically relevant problem of predicting acute radiation toxicity to facilitate treatment planning modifications and toxicity management. Clear translational pathway to clinical implementation. However, paper is explicitly designated feasibility study; authors state further investigations required to determine generalizability. No clinical implementation or outcome modification demonstrated yet.

reporting_quality.justification: Most key STROBE elements present: clear objectives, participant selection criteria, statistical methods with cross-validation details, results with AUCs and 95% confidence intervals. Some gaps: no statement on data availability or code sharing, no trial pre-registration mentioned, limited discussion of selection bias mechanisms. Supplementary materials referenced but content not fully detailed.

novelty_literature.justification: Dosiomic analysis for radiation toxicity prediction already established in literature for various cancer sites and toxicities. Xerostomia dosiomics previously studied (references 28-30). Authors note first dysphagia dosiomic analysis but this represents incremental extension rather than novel mechanism. Multi-organ combination is somewhat novel for this specific toxicity pair but not paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction positioning the work, comprehensive methods section with appropriate technical detail. Results presented clearly with ROC curves and comparison tables. Statistical analysis explained thoroughly. Professional writing with appropriate grammatical quality. Limitations section thorough and honest about constraints.

key_strengths: First comprehensive multi-organ dosiomic analysis for both xerostomia and dysphagia in HNC radiotherapy with clear clinical decision-support application

Rigorous machine learning approach with proper leave-one-out cross-validation, feature selection pipeline with multicollinearity correction, and appropriate statistical testing with Bonferroni correction
Addresses real gap in literature by investigating oral cavity contribution to xerostomia beyond parotid/submandibular focus
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=44) from single center limits statistical stability and generalizability; feasibility study designation acknowledges this limitation
No external validation; results require confirmation in independent cohort before clinical implementation
Unclear clinical benefit over existing DVH-based NTCP models; some toxicities show no significant improvement with dosiomic approach versus DVH alone
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent feasibility study with appropriate methodology but constrained by small sample size and single-center design. Tier 3 suitable for preliminary findings requiring external validation and larger cohort confirmation before clinical adoption.
